options.why: Added $1$ to the positive root $n = 10$, incorrectly treating it as $n - 1$, giving $10 + 1 = 11$.

questions.question_text: Find the number of terms of the series $20 + 18 + 16 + \dots$ required to make the partial sum $S_n = 0$.

options.why: Omitted the $-1$ in $(n - 1)d$, giving $0 = \dfrac{n}{2}(40 - 2n) = n(20 - n)$ and the incorrect positive root $n = 20$.
Gave the trivial root $n = 0$ instead of the positive solution.
Added $1$ extra term beyond the zero sum.

questions.question_text: For the decreasing series $15 + 13 + 11 + \dots$, which two values of $n$ give a partial sum of $63$?

options.why: Selected integers that sum to $16$ but have a product different from $63$.
Chose symmetrical values around $8$ that do not satisfy the quadratic.
Omitted the second valid positive integer solution.

questions.question_text: How many terms of the arithmetic series $5 + 9 + 13 + \dots$ must be summed to equal $230$?

options.why: Added $1$ to the positive root $n = 10$, incorrectly treating it as $n - 1$, giving $10 + 1 = 11$.
Took the magnitude of the numerator of the rejected root $-23/2$ and omitted division by $2$, giving $23$.
Copied the required sum as $152$ instead of $230$, giving $2n^2 + 3n - 152 = (n - 8)(2n + 19) = 0$ and the incorrect positive root $n = 8$.

questions.question_text: Find the least number of terms of the series $36 + 31 + 26 + \dots$ for which the partial sum $S_n$ is negative.

options.why: Found the last term for which the sum is still non-negative ($S_{15} \ge 0$).
Added an extra term beyond the minimal threshold.
Omitted the $-1$ in $(n - 1)d$, obtaining $72 - 5n < 0$ and $n > 14.4$, then incorrectly truncated $14.4$ to $14$.

questions.question_text:
An arithmetic series has $d = 2$, last term $l = 25$, and sum $S_n = 168$.
Find all possible numbers of terms $n$.

options.why: Omitted the valid root $n = 12$; both roots are positive integers and satisfy the givens.
Averaged the two roots, giving $(12 + 14)/2 = 13$, which does not satisfy the sum equation.
Rejected $n = 14$ because its first term is $a = -1$, although the question does not require a positive first term.

questions.solution_text:
$a_n = a + (n - 1)d \implies 25 = a + 2(n - 1) \implies a = 27 - 2n$
$S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l) \implies 168 = \dfrac{n}{2}(27 - 2n + 25)$
$336 = n(52 - 2n)$
$n^2 - 26n + 168 = 0$
$(n - 12)(n - 14) = 0$
$n = 12 \text{ or } n = 14$
For $n = 12$, $a = 3$; for $n = 14$, $a = -1$. Both term counts are positive integers and satisfy the given last term and sum, so all possible counts are $12$ and $14$.
